senses.definition: (countable) A pigeon, especially one smaller in size and white-colored; a bird (often arbitrarily called either a pigeon or a dove or both) of more than 300 species of the family Columbidae.

quotes.text: Dove's brains have been prepared by chefs for amorous expectations.
quotes.reference: 1961, Harry E. Wedeck, Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs, New York: The Citadel Press, page 77:

senses.definition: (countable, politics) A person favouring conciliation and negotiation rather than conflict.

quotes.text: On the left are the activist Vietniks, eager to protest the war; next are the doves, who oppose the U.S. role but shun demonstrations; and in the middle are the apathetics, who simply are not concerned enough to think through their own stand.
quotes.reference: 1965 November 19, “Universities: The Spectrum on Viet Nam”, in Time, volume 86, number 21, page 67:

senses.definition: (countable) Term of endearment for one regarded as pure and gentle.

quotes.text: O my dove, […] let me hear thy voice.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Song of Solomon 2:14:

senses.definition: A greyish, bluish, pinkish colour like that of the bird.
(slang, countable) Ellipsis of love dove (“tablet of the drug ecstasy”).
(chiefly Canada, US; dialectal in the UK) simple past of dive
examples:
2007: Bob Harris, Who Hates Whom: Well-Armed Fanatics, Intractable Conflicts, and Various Things Blowing up: A Woefully Incomplete Guide, §: Africa, Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Côte d’Ivoire, page 80, ¶ 4 (first edition; Three Rivers Press; →ISBN
